$comment: Declarative source of truth for scripts-utilities. Consumed by modules/*.ps1 (via lib/catalog.ps1), scripts/install-machine-scope.ps1, gui/toolbox-gui.ps1, and (later) the uninstaller. Stage-1 toolbox contents live in scripts/build-devtoolbox.ps1 and are NOT described here (the toolbox_layers block that claimed to was never read by anything - the real switches are -SkipHeavy and -SkipPlaywrightBrowsers on that script). Keep machine_scope_ids in sync with the machineScope entries in build-devtoolbox.ps1. schema_version is validated by Get-Catalog in lib/catalog.ps1: bump both together.

tools.name: gh
tools.notes: GitHub CLI - auth, PRs, issues, releases

tools.name: pwsh
tools.notes: PowerShell 7 side by side with Windows PowerShell 5.1; installer_type=wix is REQUIRED - winget 7.6.0+ defaults this id to the MSIX, which is single-user, sandboxes $PSHOME and cannot set machine-wide execution policy. CI runners use the MSI, so the MSI is what reproduces them. The wix installer is machine-scope only: --installer-type wix --scope user returns 0x8A150010.

tools.name: fzf
tools.notes: fuzzy finder for interactive CLI selection

tools.name: bat
tools.notes: syntax-highlighted file pager

tools.name: git-delta
tools.notes: syntax-highlighted diff viewer; set as git core.pager

tools.name: just
tools.notes: task runner (Justfile); cross-platform parity with Linux just

tools.name: hyperfine
tools.notes: benchmark runner and CLI timer

tools.name: sops
tools.notes: encrypted YAML/JSON/env secrets management; pairs with age

tools.name: age
tools.notes: modern file encryption; age-keygen generates recipient keys

tools.name: tokei
tools.notes: code statistics and LOC counter

tools.name: podman
tools.notes: daemonless OCI container engine. winget-default is deliberate: the Podman.CLI manifest declares no scope, so BOTH --scope user and --scope machine fail with 0x8A150010 'No applicable installer found' (verified as user and as SYSTEM). With no --scope flag it installs per-user to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Podman and adds itself to the USER PATH - no elevation, no system PATH entry. Linux containers need a VM: `podman machine init --provider hyperv` (Hyper-V feature + Hyper-V Administrators membership, admin for the first init only) or the default WSL provider. Pair with docker-compose for full compose-spec fidelity.

tools.name: docker-compose
tools.notes: standalone Compose v2 binary. Drives Podman over its Docker-compatible API pipe (npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine) - preferred over podman-compose because it is the reference Compose implementation (profiles, ${VAR:-default}, depends_on, project name all behave identically).

tools.name: curl-libressl
tools.notes: curl built against LibreSSL instead of Schannel. Windows' bundled C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe uses Schannel, whose AcquireCredentialsHandle fails with SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS inside sandboxed agent runners (see docs/agent-rules.md 'Native HTTPS in agent sandboxes'). This build does TLS in userspace and ships its own curl-ca-bundle.crt, so it works there. Detection uses trurl because System32 curl.exe wins bare-name PATH resolution and would mask a missing install; call this curl.exe by absolute path from its package bin dir.

tools.name: yt-dlp
tools.notes: video/audio downloader (actively maintained youtube-dl fork; supports 1000+ sites). Auto-discovers the toolbox's ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH, so stream-merging (-f bestvideo+bestaudio), audio extraction (-x --audio-format mp3), and remuxing work with no separate ffmpeg install. YouTube needs a JavaScript runtime to solve nsig/PO-token challenges (extraction fails otherwise): the EJS solver SCRIPTS are already bundled in this PyInstaller standalone binary, but the RUNTIME is not - install `deno` (its own catalog entry) and yt-dlp auto-detects it. Refresh the bundled solver between releases with `--remote-components ejs:github`. Self-updates via `yt-dlp -U`, but winget owns this copy - prefer `winget upgrade yt-dlp.yt-dlp` to stay channel-clean.

tools.name: deno
tools.notes: secure JavaScript/TypeScript runtime. Also serves as yt-dlp's JS challenge runtime: yt-dlp enables deno by DEFAULT, auto-detects it on PATH, and runs its bundled EJS scripts under Deno's restricted permissions to solve YouTube nsig/PO-token challenges. Without a JS runtime, YouTube downloads are blocked. yt-dlp requires deno >=2.3. Node (already in the toolbox, >=22) also works but is not default - opt in per-call/config with `--js-runtimes node`.

tools.name: tshark
tools.notes: CLI packet analysis (Wireshark backend); GUI at wireshark.exe

tools.name: etl2pcapng
tools.notes: convert pktmon/netsh-trace .etl captures to .pcapng for tshark/Wireshark (driver-free capture path)

tools.name: frida
tools.notes: dynamic instrumentation toolkit (toolbox venv)

tools.name: markdownlint-cli
tools.notes: markdown linter, and the markdown half of lib/GateChecks.ps1's six repo checks. PINNED to 0.48.0, and the pin is the point: .github/workflows/gate.yml installs that exact version, so an unpinned local install lets a minor release add a rule and make the LOCAL gate stricter than CI on unchanged documentation - a failure nobody can reproduce from the repo. Measured 2026-09-17 against 0.48.0: findings go to STDERR with an EMPTY stdout (a stdout-only capture reports clean while exiting 1), the tool exits 0 and prints its usage banner when its arguments match no file (which is why the check carries a floor), and a bad config path exits 4. Those three behaviours are what scripts/run-gate-checks.ps1 and ConvertFrom-GCMarkdownlintOutput are written against; re-measure them before moving the pin. Note that Install-NpmGlobal short-circuits on the BINARY being present, not on its version, so changing this pin does not upgrade an existing install - uninstall first, or run npm install -g explicitly. The runner prints the version it used on every gate run, so a skew is visible in the log rather than mysterious.

tools.name: jupyterlab
tools.notes: Jupyter notebook server (toolbox venv); launch with 'jupyter-lab'

tools.name: sqlite-utils
tools.notes: SQLite CLI automation: insert, query, transform, export

tools.name: csvkit
tools.notes: CSV utilities: csvlook, csvcut, csvstat, csvjoin, in2csv, sql2csv

tools.name: pytoshop
tools.notes: write layered Photoshop .psd files from Python (import-only; no CLI)

tools.name: trafilatura
tools.notes: main-content extraction for the `browse` CLI (tools/browse, installed by scripts/install-browse.ps1). OPTIONAL: browse falls back to a bs4+lxml extractor when this is absent and prints a DEGRADED line on every run saying so, so a box without it still works and still tells you. default:false because it pulls a handful of transitive deps (courlan, htmldate, justext, dateparser) into the SHARED venv; none of them pin numpy or pillow, which is the pairing that has broken rembg/scikit-image/pdfplumber here before, but check before adding more. Quality difference is real: bs4 returns the whole cleaned body, trafilatura finds the article column.

tools.name: curl_cffi
tools.notes: HTTP client with a real browser TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint, used by the `browse` CLI's first rung when present. OPTIONAL, and browse says so on every run when it is missing. Worth having for the reason a May 2026 benchmark measured: curl_cffi scored 26 OK / 2 blocked over 31 anti-bot targets, tying a 130 MB patched Chromium fork from a 6.4 MB wheel, because the TLS handshake and HTTP/2 frame order are what the gate cross-checks - and httpx cannot change either. Import-only here (its CLI is not used), hence register_manifest:false.

tools.name: cuda-toolkit
tools.notes: CUDA 13 toolkit, needed for onnxruntime-gpu's CUDAExecutionProvider (1.30 requires CUDA 13.* + cuDNN 9.*; torch's bundled CUDA 12 does NOT satisfy it, the provider just fails to load). CUDA 13 moved the runtime DLLs to bin/x64 rather than bin - cudart64_13.dll and cublasLt64_13.dll live there, and that directory must be on PATH (add_dll_directory alone is not enough) or onnxruntime falls back to CPU SILENTLY and is merely ~20x slower. Pair with nvidia-cudnn-cu13. default:false because it is ~4 GB and only GPU inference needs it.

tools.name: nvidia-cudnn-cu13
tools.notes: cuDNN 9 for CUDA 13; DLLs only, no import module, lands in site-packages/nvidia/cudnn/bin. Required by onnxruntime-gpu next to the CUDA 13 toolkit. Note the nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu13 wheel on PyPI is a 1.2 kB 0.0.0a0 placeholder - take the runtime from the toolkit, not pip. Safe to install with its deps: it pulls nvidia-cublas and nvidia-cuda-nvrtc but touches no numpy/pillow pins. Unrelated ML packages often DO pin those - use pip --no-deps for those, or they downgrade numpy/pillow and break rembg, scikit-image, pdfplumber and pillow-heif in this shared venv.

tools.name: ollama
tools.notes: local LLM runtime; per-user background service at 127.0.0.1:11434 (OpenAI-compatible). Installed by scripts/install-llm.ps1, not the default groups.

machine_scope_overrides.$comment: Per-package winget overrides for scripts/install-machine-scope.ps1, keyed by winget id. no_scope_flag=true means omit --scope entirely and let winget use the package's own default, which for these packages IS machine scope: the WDK returns 0x8A150010 when --scope machine is passed even though it installs to machine-scope paths. This lived as a hardcoded $NoScopeFlag array in the script, which could disagree with machine_scope_ids here without anything noticing. Keyed by id rather than set on a tools[] entry because 7 of the 10 machine_scope_ids - the WDK among them - have NO tools[] entry at all (they are stage-1 natives from scripts/build-devtoolbox.ps1), so a tools[] field would have been unreachable for the only id that needs it. machine_scope_ids itself stays a flat array of strings: install-machine-scope.ps1 and scripts/smoke-test.ps1 both index it that way. Keys beginning with $ are comments, not package ids.

llm.$comment: Optional local-LLM stack, provisioned by scripts/install-llm.ps1 (opt-in, not a default group). Ollama is the only runtime implemented; llama.cpp is an opt-in alternative (see BACKLOG) and is NOT selectable from here. Model pulls are VRAM-tiered so an 8 GB box does not waste disk on models it cannot run. There is no embedding-fallback list: nothing implements one, and the two models it used to name were not in models_base, so it read as a capability that did not exist.

reranker.name: bge-reranker-base
reranker.notes: cross-encoder reranker run via the toolbox onnxruntime (not Ollama)

side_effects.$comment: Inventory of everything the toolbox mutates, so the uninstaller can reverse it. Paths under path_entries_relative are relative to the toolbox root (CODEX_TOOLBOX or %LOCALAPPDATA%\DevToolbox).
side_effects.$comment_machine: Entries scripts\consolidate-path.ps1 moves into the MACHINE hive. They are listed SEPARATELY from path_entries_relative because reversing them needs a different API and elevation: Remove-UserPathEntry silently does nothing to an HKLM entry, which is why the uninstaller used to claim a clean reversal while leaving both of these behind. Removing them is idempotent - the uninstaller asks for both regardless of scope, and an entry present only in the user hive is reported NotPresent here and removed by path_entries_relative above.
